def:hq-bi-filtration:
Definition Knot-indexed bi-filtration \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} on the aether convolution algebra. Let \mathcal{H}_q be the aether convolution Hopf algebra (Frobenius–Hopf aether), filtered by iterated-integral depth G^{(0)} \subseteq G^{(1)} \subseteq \cdots. For each Bring-embeddable knot/link K (Bring-embeddable knots) with dominant cell \lambda_K \vdash n_K and central primitive idempotent e_{\lambda_K} \in Z(H_{n_K}(q)) (explicit central idempotent), the knot-K-localised depth-n stratum is

  \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}
  \;:=\;
  \bigl\{\, \alpha \;\in\; G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q)
        \;:\; e_{\lambda_K} \cdot \alpha \cdot e_{\lambda_K} = \alpha \,\bigr\}.

The double-indexed family \{\mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}\}_{n \geq 0,\;K} is the bi-filtration: a horizontal axis of iterated-integral depth n (Goncharov side) and a vertical axis of knot/braid class K (Hecke cell side).

Axes and refinements

Depth axis n (horizontal). G^{(0)} contains \exp_q and scalars; G^{(n)} adjoins the grouplikes \log_q, \mathrm{Li}_2^q, \ldots, \mathrm{Li}_n^q. Compatible with \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} via \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(n)}) \subseteq \mathcal{P}_n.

Knot axis K (vertical). Refined by partition cell \lambda_K. Two natural sub-axes inside the K-axis:

  1. Bar-class. Self-conjugate \lambda_K = \lambda_K' vs chiral pair \lambda_K \neq \lambda_K' (cf. Chirality structure on Goncharov period classes via the bar involution).
  2. Genus. g(K) \leq 4 for Bring-embeddable (Bring-embeddable knots: genus-bounded table and per-knot witness targets for the depth correspondence).

Compatibility with the Hopf and braid structures

The bi-filtration interacts with the existing structures on \mathcal{H}_q:

conj:joint-galois-braid-action:
Conjecture Joint motivic-Galois \times braid-group action on the bi-filtration \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}. Let \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} be the knot-indexed bi-filtration (Knot-indexed bi-filtration \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} on the aether convolution algebra). Two groups act on it by symmetry:

  • the motivic Galois group G_{\mathrm{mot}} acts on the depth axis, permuting Goncharov period classes \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} (Kontsevich–Zagier 2001, Goncharov 2001);
  • the braid group B_{n_K} acts on the knot axis, permuting Wedderburn cells e_{\lambda_K} via the standard representation on H_{n_K}(q).

Conjectural joint structure: these two actions extend to a joint action of a semi-direct product G_{\mathrm{mot}} \rtimes B_{n_K} on \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}, with the action on each axis being equivariant with respect to the action on the other:

  \boxed{\;
    g_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta \cdot \alpha)
    \;=\;
    \beta \cdot g_{\mathrm{mot}}(\alpha)
    \quad\text{for } \alpha \in \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)},\;
    g_{\mathrm{mot}} \in G_{\mathrm{mot}},\;
    \beta \in B_{n_K}.
  \;}

Equivalently: the motivic-Galois action commutes with the braid- group action when restricted to the bi-filtration, and the joint group G_{\mathrm{mot}} \times B_{n_K} stabilises each \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} stratum.

Structural motivation for the prediction

Three motivations:

  1. The depth axis is Galois-equivariant by construction. Goncharov's motivic-Galois group acts accordingly on the period algebra \mathcal{P}_*, preserving the depth filtration. Pulled back via \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, this gives an action on each G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q).

  2. The knot axis is braid-equivariant by construction. The braid group B_n acts on H_n(q) via the standard half-twist generators \sigma_i, permuting Wedderburn cells via the Hoefsmit seminormal-form action. This descends to an action on \mathcal{H}_q via Schur–Weyl.

  3. The two actions touch different parts of the structure. Galois acts on q-coefficients (via q \mapsto q^{-1} for the bar involution, or via cyclotomic Galois on \zeta_n); braid acts on the Hecke-element argument. These are a priori orthogonal, so commutativity is the natural conjecture.

Equivalent statements

  • The bi-filtration \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} is a bi-graded (G_{\mathrm{mot}} \times B_{n_K})-module.
  • The composition map \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} \circ (\beta \cdot -) equals (\beta \cdot -) \circ \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} on each stratum (with \beta acting on the period side via its monodromy representation).
  • The joint orbit of any \alpha \in \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} under G_{\mathrm{mot}} \times B_{n_K} stays within \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}.

Concrete prediction at (n, K) = (3, \zeta_5\text{-Bring})

For the Bring depth-3 bi-filtration cell (Bring trilog at \zeta_5 as depth-3 grouplike value (50-digit functional-equation cross-validated witness)):

  • G_{\mathrm{mot}}-action: cyclotomic Galois \sigma_a \colon \zeta_5 \mapsto \zeta_5^a for \gcd(a, 5) = 1. Permutes \{\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k) : k = 1, 2, 3, 4\} as the (\mathbb{Z}/5)^\times \cong \mathbb{Z}/4 orbit.
  • B_n-action (here B_5 via S_5 symmetry of Bring): permutes the same 4 values via the regular representation of S_5 on \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5).

The conjecture predicts: these two permutation actions commute. Numerical evidence: the orbit-sum \sum_{k=1}^4 \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k) = -\frac{24}{25}\zeta(3) is both Galois-invariant (= cyclotomic Galois-trace) and S_5-invariant (= regular-representation trace), so the joint- invariant subspace contains \zeta(3). Higher invariants would test the joint commutativity sharply.

Concrete prediction at (n, K) = (2, 4_1)

For the figure-8 (\lambda_K = (2, 2) self-conjugate cell):

  • G_{\mathrm{mot}}-action: bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1}. Fixes e_{(2, 2)} since (2, 2) is self-conjugate; it acts as the identity on \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \in \mathcal{P}_2^+.
  • B_3-action (figure-8 is a 3-strand braid): the dihedral D_3 = S_3 symmetry of the braid acts trivially on e_{(2, 2)} (since (2, 2) is the unique self-conjugate cell of H_3 \subset H_4 structure).

Joint action stabilises the entire stratum trivially — consistent with the prediction that the figure-8 is the canonical fixed point for both groups in \mathcal{H}_q^{(2, K)}.

Significance

If discharged, the joint action gives:

  1. Symmetry-organised period generation. Periods at depth n for knot K generate a G_{\mathrm{mot}} \rtimes B_{n_K}-module; the irreducible decomposition predicts which periods are independent vs forced by q-rational structure.
  2. Cross-axis dictionaries. Galois orbits on \mathcal{P}_n correspond to braid orbits on cells: each pair (g, \beta) gives a relation among period values.
  3. Sharpness of the depth correspondence via representation theory. The correspondence's sharpness condition (image generates \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} non-trivially) reduces to non-vanishing of certain G_{\mathrm{mot}} \rtimes B_n-invariants — a representation- theoretic question, much more tractable than transcendence-theoretic ones.

  \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}
  \;:\;
  \widehat{\mathcal{M}}

  \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \otimes_{K_0(\mathrm{Var})} \mathbb{Z}

rem:archimedean-realization-functor-inte:
Remark Archimedean realization: functor vs. motivic measure and identification with \tau. Realization and projection. A motivic integral \int_{\mathcal{L}(X)} d\mu \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} defines a geometric shape. The topological realization \chi_{\mathrm{top}} maps this shape to an integer (Euler characteristic) or a refined Hodge-theoretic invariant like hyperbolic volume. The adelic projection \pi_\infty discards non-archimedean components, returning the real-valued laboratory measurement.

Level of the construction (functor vs. motivic measure). As written, \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} has domain the Grothendieck ring \widehat{\mathcal{M}} = K_0(\mathrm{Var})^{\wedge}, and \chi_{\mathrm{top}} \colon K_0(\mathrm{Var}) \to \mathbb{Z} is a ring homomorphism — a motivic measure in the sense of Denef–Loeser — while \pi_\infty is an archimedean place. A map out of a ring is not a functor between categories: "functor" is literally accurate only for the fibre functor \tau (below), or when the domain is lifted to the category of motives \mathrm{DM}(k), where Betti/Hodge realization is a bona fide functor. On \widehat{\mathcal{M}} itself, \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} is the archimedean realization / evaluation into \mathbb{R}, not a functor between QOU categories — consistent with the notation register, which reserves "functor" for \tau and treats the R \mapsto \mathbb{R} realization as an evaluation. The block label is retained for stability.

Identification with the fibre functor. The QOU fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Arch} is the exclusive exit from the categorical aether to the real numbers. On motivic QOU inputs, \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} coincides exactly with the archimedean component of \tau:

  \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}
  \;=\;
  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}
  \;:=\;
  \pi_\infty \circ \tau
  \quad\text{on } \widehat{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{QOU}}
  \;\subseteq\; \widehat{\mathcal{M}}.

Synthesis. The framework processes discrete categorical data along a single chain: adelic stitching, motivic integration, and archimedean projection. It requires no continuous differential equations or Lebesgue measures. The Kashaev limit of the algebraic quantum volume exemplifies this mechanism.
prop:archimedean-functor-uniqueness:
Proposition Uniqueness of the archimedean realization functor (Bloch-Suslin pentagon, conditional). Conditional on (1{-}q)\,\log\Phi_n(x; q) \to \mathrm{Li}_2(x) under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} and on the Bloch-Suslin pentagon-uniqueness theorem [suslin1991]. Let \tau_{\text{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau be the archimedean realization functor of the QOU aether (archimedean realization functor), acting on motivic inputs assembled from braid / knot data. Under hypotheses (C1)–(C2) below, \tau_{\text{arch}} is uniquely determined, up to a single multiplicative real scalar, by the requirement that

  \lim_{q \to 1}\;\tau_{\text{arch}}\bigl(\Phi_q(z)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  D(z)
  \;:=\;
  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(z) + \log|z|\,\arg(1-z)

equal the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm on every shape parameter z \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0,1\}, where:

  • (C1) The aether's mass-formula state sum is pentagon-coherent: \tau_{\text{arch}} is a continuous, antisymmetric, real-valued functional on B(\mathbb{C}) — the structural content provided by the cosimplicial / Yekutieli triple machinery (Cosimplicial crossed groupoid) together with the archimedean limit assumed in the opening banner.
  • (C2) Bloch-Suslin pentagon-uniqueness [suslin1991, bloch2000]: any continuous antisymmetric pentagon-coherent real-valued function on \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0,1\} is a constant scalar multiple of the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm D.

The uniqueness reduces to the Bloch-Suslin pentagon characterisation: D is the unique (up to a real scalar) continuous, antisymmetric, real-valued function on \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0,1\} satisfying the 5-term pentagon identity

  D(x) - D(y) + D\!\left(\tfrac{y}{x}\right)
  - D\!\left(\tfrac{1-y^{-1}}{1-x^{-1}}\right)
  + D\!\left(\tfrac{1-y}{1-x}\right) \;=\; 0.

Theorem (conditional on (1{-}q)\,\log\Phi_n(x; q) \to \mathrm{Li}_2(x) under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}). The upstream archimedean-limit conjecture is taken as a hypothesis, and the Bloch-Suslin pentagon-uniqueness theorem [suslin1991, bloch2000] is likewise taken as a hypothesis (cited, not re-proved). The uniqueness statement is proved from these two hypotheses alone, and therefore qualifies as a rigorous conditional result rather than an unproved conjecture.

rem:two-filtration-bridge-general-argume:
Remark Argument for two filtration bridge general (not a proof).

Proof — bar-eigenspace argument

Step 1 (which involution transposes \lambda). The bar involution does not transpose cells. It fixes every central primitive idempotent:

  \mathrm{bar}(e_\lambda) \;=\; e_\lambda .

Bar is a ring automorphism of H_n(q), so it permutes the e_\lambda. At q = 1 it is T_w \mapsto T_{w^{-1}}^{-1} = T_w, the identity, and the permutation is locally constant in q, so it is the identity. Explicitly in H_2 (with \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h, h = q - q^{-1}), e_{(2)} = (\sigma + q^{-1})/(q + q^{-1}) maps to (\sigma - h + q)/(q^{-1} + q) = e_{(2)}.

The involution that transposes is the Goldman involution \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1}, which is q-linear and at q = 1 is tensoring with the sign character:

  \#(e_\lambda) \;=\; e_{\lambda'} .

In H_2, \#(e_{(2)}) = (-\sigma + h + q^{-1})/(q + q^{-1}) = (q - \sigma)/(q + q^{-1}) = e_{(1,1)}. In particular, \mathrm{bar}(e_\lambda) \neq e_{\lambda'} whenever \lambda \neq \lambda'. Steps 2 and 3 below require the cell-transposing involution, so on the Hecke side orientation reversal pairs with \# rather than \mathrm{bar}.

Step 2 (period-class bar-action). Under the archimedean realization functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} (Archimedean realization functor \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}), the bar involution acts on the period side by:

  • Hyperbolic volume: \mathrm{Vol}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(\overline{K}) — bar-INVARIANT (orientation-reversal preserves the metric). Lives in \mathcal{P}_2^+ (real, bar-fixed).
  • Chern–Simons: \mathrm{CS}(K) = -\mathrm{CS}(\overline{K}) mod \pi^2 \mathbb{Z} — bar-ANTI-INVARIANT (CS picks up the orientation sign). Lives in \mathcal{P}_3^- (Tate-twisted).

These are the two characteristic period-class bar-types at depths 2 and 3 respectively.

Step 3 (pairing analysis).

Self-conjugate case \lambda = \lambda'. \#(e_\lambda) = e_\lambda — the cell is \#-fixed. Pairing with a depth-n grouplike g \in G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q) under Markov trace yields a value in the bar-fixed component of \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n - 1}:

  • At n = 2: pairs with \mathrm{Vol} (bar-fixed), which can be non-zero.
  • At n = 3: pairs with \mathrm{CS} (bar-anti-fixed) — gives zero on bar-fixed cells.

So bar-fixed cell \Rightarrow d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) = 2.

Chiral pair case \lambda \neq \lambda'. \#(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda'} — \# swaps the two cells, so e_\lambda itself is not an eigenvector: it is the sum of its symmetric and antisymmetric parts below, both nonzero. The bar-eigenspaces of the direct sum e_\lambda + e_{\lambda'} decompose as:

  • Bar-symmetric: (e_\lambda + e_{\lambda'})/2 — pairs with depth-2 (Vol-type) periods.
  • Bar-antisymmetric: (e_\lambda - e_{\lambda'})/2 — pairs with depth-3 (CS-type) periods, if the matching holds.

The bar-symmetric part pairs by definition with depth-2 of a chiral knot (volume can be non-zero, but in the chiral pair the antisymmetric content carries the orientation-dependent signature). The bar-antisymmetric part is the natural pairing partner of \mathrm{CS} (which is bar-anti-invariant).

So chiral pair \Rightarrow d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) = 3.

What this argument does not prove. Steps 2 and 3 assume that \# on the Hecke side matches orientation reversal on the period side, and that "pairing with a depth-n grouplike" lands in the matching eigenspace. Neither is proved here, and d_{\mathrm{II}} itself is defined only through Two-filtration bridge: iterated-integral depth \leftrightarrow partition-cellular GB-depth via e_\lambda. The argument is therefore a heuristic, conditional on that conjecture and on this matching. The part that is a theorem is item 4 of Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q)): under (H-match) and (H-parity) it gives the vanishing and antisymmetry of odd-depth components, but not the non-vanishing that the values 2 and 3 require. Assigning a single depth to a chiral cell is not forced, because e_\lambda carries both a symmetric and an antisymmetric part.

Generality of the proof

The argument is structural, not case-by-case:

  1. No upper bound on n. Works for partitions of any size.
  2. Bar-class of \lambda is computable. Self-conjugate partitions of n are exactly those with bar-fixed Young diagram (a well-defined combinatorial property).
  3. Depth assignment is binary by definition. The values 2 and 3 come from the definition of d_{\mathrm{II}}, whose third branch is empty.

See Table.

(Self-conjugate partitions of n are in bijection with partitions of n into distinct odd parts — a classical result.)
rem:adelic-base-ring-integration:
Remark Motivation for the adelic base ring and Tate integration. Each non-archimedean place p corresponds to a localized quantum geometric state of the aether: a specific q-deformation evaluated at a primitive root of unity, equivalently a Kummer level in the Habiro / cyclotomic completion (algebraic quantum volume). The archimedean place \infty — the \mathbb{R} component — is the laboratory continuum.

Motivation for the adelic base ring. Replacing \mathbb{R} by \mathbb{A} resolves a structural tension: the local q-geometries at each prime do not assemble into a continuous manifold, but they do assemble into a global adelic object. The macroscopic universe is therefore not the real continuum \mathbb{R} alone but the simultaneous integration of all local non-archimedean data weighted by their archimedean shadow.

Adelic integration (Tate's thesis). Global observables of the aether — the macroscopic mass functional, the global L-function of Bring's coordinate ring, the partition functions of the brane tower — are not Riemann integrals over \mathbb{R}. They are Tate integrals over \mathbb{A}:

  \mathcal{Z}(s)
  \;=\;
  \int_{\mathbb{A}^\times} \! f(x)\,|x|^s\, d^\times x
  \;=\;
  \zeta_\infty(s) \cdot \prod_{p} \zeta_p(s),

a product of local zeta integrals, one per place. The classical \zeta(s) is recovered as the global Tate integral of the standard adelic Schwartz function. Local q-zeta data and macroscopic real-valued observables are two faces of the same adelic object.

Discrete quantum data at every prime is glued by adelic restriction and projected to physical numbers by the archimedean realization functor.
rem:motivic-base-ring-canonicity:
Remark Canonicity, realizations, and scope of the motivic base ring. Canonicity of the aether. Three observations factor through \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mot}} rather than any single realization:

  • Mass formulas. The topological mass of a knot (motivic mass measure) is a class \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta) \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}}, not a real number. The real-valued mass arises only after applying \rho_\infty.
  • Adelic factorisation. The global zeta integral \mathcal{Z}(s) of the adelic base ring factorises as a restricted product \prod_v \zeta_v(s). This is the realization-tower factorisation \rho_{\mathrm{tot}} = \prod_v \rho_v applied to a single motivic class.
  • Habiro evaluation. The Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} is the universal target of the non-archimedean realizations of \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mot}}. The functor \rho_p evaluates a motivic class at the level-p root of unity. The inverse limit over p recovers the Habiro completion.

Every algebraic invariant taking values in \mathbb{R}, \mathbb{Q}_p, or the Habiro ring is the realization at some place v of a single motivic class living in \widehat{\mathcal{M}}.

Relation to existing blocks.

  • The Frobenius–Hopf aether is the algebraic-place realization. It forms a finite-type structure on \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mot}}.
  • The arc space \mathcal{L}(X) provides the measurable space for motivic integration into \widehat{\mathcal{M}}. One derives the Kontsevich–Denef–Loeser motivic measure [kontsevich1995, denef-loeser2001] from this space.

Out of scope. Mixed motives, Bloch–Kato exact sequences, and full motivic Galois groups are not axiomatized here. The realization tower is presented purely as the family \{\rho_v\} of place-indexed evaluations; the categorical relationships among the \rho_v remain implicit.
rem:q-clt-jsj-mass-scaling:
Remark q-CLT / JSJ volume scaling for heavy isotopes. When modeling the macroscopic atomic mass of heavy isotopes up to Oganesson (A=294), evaluating the absolute topological Hecke trace of the A-nucleon knot becomes computationally intractable. The Jaco–Shalen–Johannson (JSJ) decomposition glues the atomic knot complement along essential (inter-nucleon) tori, and hyperbolic volume is additive under torus gluing. The leading mass term is therefore volume-additive — linear in the nucleon counts:

\mathfrak{m}_{\text{qCLT,lead}}(Z, N) = Z\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}}.

Accordingly the absolute mass prediction splits into two computational channels:

  1. Symbolic channel: the exact closed-form evaluation of the Hecke matrix traces, computationally constrained to light isotopes (A \le 8).
  2. q-CLT channel: the JSJ-additive estimator Z\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - B(Z,N), where B is the binding energy (the \Delta_\lambda correction).

The additive structure is exact: the inter-nucleon tori make the volume — hence the leading mass term — linear in (Z,N). The absolute prediction depends on two residuals: the binding fraction B/\mathfrak{m} (which plateaus near 0.9\% under nuclear saturation, so it does not vanish for heavy A) and the nucleon-mass gap. The nucleon-mass gap is +2.89\% in the proved pipeline (the production linking weight); the derived, no-fit spectral-phase correction \theta/(8\hbar_q^2)\approx 0.9711 reduces it \sim 35\times to -819 ppm, but is exploratory and not part of the production route (its "why \theta/(8\hbar_q^2)" step is unproved). Validated on the three light compound nuclei where B is available (D, T, {}^3\mathrm{He}), the binding-corrected channel reproduces the CODATA atomic mass to within the nucleon-mass gap, uniformly across isotopes — production residual \approx 2.89\% (cross-isotope spread 0.014\%), spectral residual \approx -800 ppm. The uniformity is the signature that the additive structure is sound; the asymptotic claim is about the linear structure, not absolute exactness.

The binding B admits two evaluations in this channel: the framework's per-isotope \Delta_\lambda prediction, and a self-contained factorized q-CLT binding B = \alpha \sum_i \ln\lvert V_i\rvert, with the derived scale \alpha = \mathfrak{m}_e/\!\left(q_0(q_0-1)\right) (fixed by q_0 and the electron mass alone — not Q_\beta, not a fit) and each V_i the Markov-trace ratio of a two-nucleon sub-braid for one bond type (p–p, p–n, n–n). Because the n–n bond is more suppressing than the p–p bond, this form resolves the {}^3\mathrm{H}/{}^3\mathrm{He} isospin splitting — which the isospin-blind leading term cannot — to within 1.1\times of the AME binding energy with no fit. prose:intro-hoefsmit-convergence-atomic:
Evaluating the mass functional across the infinite brane tower requires controlling the convergence of trace series as the strand count and jet degree grow. In the Hoefsmit basis, the Jucys–Murphy operators act diagonally by q-contents, turning the trace expansion into a content-graded series over standard Young tableaux. This section formulates operator selection as a linear program (and its semidefinite lift) over the Frobenius Gram matrix, establishes the universal braid-branching identity and its eigenvalue product expansion, and proves the Hecke convergence bound.

The algebraic home of these convergent trace series is the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} and its two-variable extension, the z-Habiro completion. Embedding the transient brane-tower terms into the z-Habiro ring ensures that cyclotomic poles cancel order by order before the archimedean realization functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} evaluates the series at q_0.
prop:operator-selection-lp:
Proposition Knot operator selection as linear program with LP duality. Let n \geq 2, let \{b_1, \ldots, b_d\} be a basis of H_n(q) (the NF basis, with d = n!), let t_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i) be the Markov traces, let G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) be the d \times d Frobenius Gram matrix, and let n_{\mathrm{target}} \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} be a target net value. Consider the linear program

  \min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} \quad \sum_{i=1}^{d} t_i \, x_i

subject to:

  \sum_{i=1}^{d} x_i = n_{\mathrm{target}}
  \qquad (\text{net constraint})
  \sum_{j=1}^{d} G_{ij}\, x_j \geq 0
  \quad \forall\, i \in \{1, \ldots, d\}
  \qquad (\text{Frobenius positivity})
  x_i \geq -M \quad \forall\, i
  \qquad (\text{boundedness})

where M > 0 is a constant large enough to ensure boundedness of the feasible polyhedron. Any minimiser \Phi^* = \sum_{i} x_i^* b_i lies in H_n(q) and satisfies every Frobenius positivity and net constraint; the dual certificate (y_0^*, y^*) certifies optimality.

Degeneracy of this program

Two properties of the program as stated, both proved and neither previously recorded. They are stated here because downstream blocks have read the program as a selection principle, which it is not.

The optimal value is identically zero. The NF basis begins with the empty word, so b_1 = \mathbf{1} and hence

G_{1j} \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}\cdot b_j) \;=\; t_j .

The first row of the Gram matrix is the objective vector, so the Frobenius positivity constraint at i = 1 reads \sum_j t_j x_j \geq 0 — the objective itself, bounded below by zero. The program therefore minimises t\cdot x subject to t\cdot x \geq 0, and its optimal value is 0 whenever it is feasible. This requires only that the basis contain the identity, so it holds for every n, every q, and every trace convention. By strong duality n_{\mathrm{target}}\cdot y_0^* = 0 with n_{\mathrm{target}} > 0, so y_0^* = 0: the net constraint carries no shadow price, and n_{\mathrm{target}} cannot influence the objective.

The set of minimisers is not a point. It is \{x : \sum_i x_i = n_{\mathrm{target}},\; (Gx)_1 = 0,\; (Gx)_i \geq 0\ (i \geq 2)\}, a positive-dimensional face. At n = 3 it carries at least six vertices, all at objective 0, occurring in mirror pairs under \sigma_0 \leftrightarrow \sigma_1. Since t and G are mirror-invariant the optimal set is mirror-closed, so a unique minimiser would have to be mirror-symmetric; none of these vertices is. The program therefore does not determine a distinguished \Phi^*, and which vertex a solver returns is a property of its pivoting rule.

Dual program (demand pricing)

The primal variable x is free apart from the box x_i \ge -M, so the dual constraints are equalities. With multipliers y_0 (free) for the net constraint, y_i \ge 0 for the Frobenius constraints and w_i \ge 0 for the box, the dual is:

  \max_{y_0,\, y,\, w} \quad n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0 - M \sum_{i=1}^{d} w_i

subject to:

  y_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{d} G_{ij}\, y_i + w_j \;=\; t_j
  \quad \forall\, j \in \{1, \ldots, d\}
  y_i \geq 0, \quad w_i \geq 0 \quad \forall\, i

If no box constraint is active at the optimum, then w^* = 0 and the dual reduces to:

  \max_{y_0, \, y \geq 0} \quad n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0

subject to:

  y_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{d} G_{ij}\, y_i \;=\; t_j
  \quad \forall\, j \in \{1, \ldots, d\}

The inequality form y_0 + \sum_i G_{ij} y_i \le t_j is the dual of the program with x \ge 0, not of this one. Because G_{1j} = t_j for b_1 = 1, the point y_0 = 0, y = e_1, w = 0 is dual-feasible with value 0, which matches the primal optimum above.

Strong duality

Proposition (strong duality). The primal and dual programs have equal optimal values:

  \sum_{i=1}^{d} t_i \, x_i^*
  \;=\;
  n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0^* - M \sum_{i=1}^{d} w_i^*,

which equals n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0^* when no box constraint is active.
prf:operator-selection-lp:
Proof Proof of operator selection lp. The feasible set is non-empty: any element \Phi_0 with \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_0) > 0 can be rescaled to satisfy the net constraint, and the Frobenius positivity constraints admit interior points (the identity \gamma = \mathbf{1} satisfies G \cdot e_1 > 0 componentwise for generic q). The boundedness constraint x_i \geq -M ensures the feasible polyhedron is bounded. By the LP strong duality theorem (no duality gap for feasible, bounded linear programs), the primal minimum equals the dual maximum.

Complementary slackness

At optimality, the complementary slackness conditions hold:

  y_i^* \cdot \left(\sum_{j=1}^{d} G_{ij}\, x_j^* \right) = 0
  \quad \forall\, i

Each dual variable y_i^* is positive only when the corresponding Frobenius constraint is tight. The set of tight constraints \mathcal{A} = \{i : y_i^* > 0\} identifies the active demand channels -- the channels that the optimal operator \Phi^* exactly saturates.

Higher-strand generalizations

For n > 3, the LP dimensions grow as d = n!:

n d = n! Physical regime
2 2 Single-particle states (photon, electron)
3 6 Baryonic confinement (proton, neutron)
4 24 Tetraquark / exotic meson candidates
5 120 Pentaquark states

At each strand number, the Frobenius Gram matrix G is symmetric, and it is non-degenerate — for q \neq 0, 1 — on the quotient H_n/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M \cong \mathrm{TL}_n, not on H_n itself, so that is where the LP is well-posed.

The LP dimension is the Catalan number C_n, not n!. Posed on all of H_n with d = n! the statement above is false: at z = q^3/(q^2+1) the weights y_\lambda vanish for every \lambda with \ell(\lambda) \geq 3, so G \in \mathbb{R}^{n! \times n!} is singular and the LP is degenerate rather than well-posed. Its rank is the surviving \sum \dim^2 = C_n:

n d = n! (as tabled) \mathrm{rank} G = C_n corank
2 2 2 0
3 6 5 1
4 24 14 10 = 3^2 + 1^2
5 120 42 78 = 6^2+5^2+4^2+1^2

So the pentaquark row is a 42-dimensional program, not a 120-dimensional one, and the tetraquark row is 14, not 24. The optimal vertex x^* and the active set \mathcal{A} are well defined on the quotient; on H_n the LP has a \mathrm{corank} G-dimensional space of optima differing by radical directions the trace cannot see.

The optimal vertex x^* identifies the minimum-action operator, and the active set \mathcal{A} identifies the saturated demand channels.

Relation to the spectral decomposition

The spectral decomposition writes \Phi = \sum_\lambda d_\lambda(q) \cdot \Phi_\lambda in the irrep basis; the LP writes \Phi = \sum_i x_i b_i in the NF basis. The two are related by the change-of-basis matrix P between the NF basis and the Wedderburn idempotent basis:

  x_i = \sum_\lambda P_{i\lambda} \, d_\lambda(q) \,
  \mathrm{tr}_\lambda(\Phi_\lambda)

The LP operates in the NF basis because the Gram matrix G_{ij} and the Markov traces t_i are directly computable from the Hecke algebra relations, without requiring explicit knowledge of the irrep decomposition. The spectral decomposition provides the physical interpretation (which knot operators mediate the interaction); the LP provides the constructive selection (which NF coefficients minimize the action).
rem:operator-selection-lp-interpretation:
Remark Economic reading of the LP dual variables. The general LP for knot operator selection in H_n(q) applies for arbitrary strand number n; the confinement LP is the special case n = 3, d = 6. The Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 is feasible for the confinement LP — its normal form satisfies every Frobenius positivity constraint strictly, \min_i (Gx)_i \approx 0.342 at the proton-anchored q_0 — but it is not a minimiser: its objective is \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_3) \approx 0.9986 against an optimal value of 0. The program does not select it, and no minimiser is distinguished (see Knot operator selection as linear program with LP duality, Degeneracy of this program).

The objective \sum_{i} t_i x_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi) is the categorical action. Minimising it does not select an operator: because b_1 = \mathbf{1}, the Frobenius positivity constraint at i = 1 is \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi) \geq 0, so the objective is bounded below by its own constraint and the minimum is identically 0. Least action here means zero action, which is attained on a whole face. The Frobenius positivity constraints Gx \geq 0 encode the demand–supply balance: \Phi must pair non-negatively with every basis element under the Frobenius inner product. No channel carries unbounded demand.

LP over motivic shadows, not real numbers. The data feeding the LP—Markov traces t_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i) and Frobenius Gram entries G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j)—are formal elements of \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}], hence elements of the Habiro completion \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. The dual variable y_0 would be the shadow price of the net constraint — the marginal cost, in units of categorical action, of increasing n_{\mathrm{target}} by one unit. In this program it is identically zero: strong duality gives n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0^* = 0 with n_{\mathrm{target}} > 0. The demand-pricing reading below therefore describes a quantity that does not vary, and n_{\mathrm{target}} acts as a pure scale. The dual variables y_i \geq 0 are the shadow prices of the Frobenius positivity constraints (channel demand prices). A positive y_i^* at optimality indicates that the i-th Frobenius constraint is tight, meaning the i-th channel is saturated.
prop:confinement-sdp:
Proposition Confinement as semidefinite program with matrix Frobenius positivity. Let n be the Hecke strand count at confinement level \ell. Let (\pi_\lambda)_{\lambda \vdash k, k \le n} be the central idempotents projecting onto the Wedderburn blocks of H_n(q). Let T be the cost operator. The confined operator at q is the solution \Phi^* \succeq 0 of the primal matrix program:

  \min_{\Phi \succeq 0} \quad \langle T, \Phi \rangle

subject to:

  1. (Per-block Frobenius positivity) \langle \pi_\lambda, \Phi \rangle \ge 0 for all \lambda \vdash k, k \le n.
  2. (Adjacent-pair PSD) Every 2 \times 2 block corresponding to an adjacent generator pair (\sigma_i, \sigma_{i+1}) is positive semi-definite.
  3. (Normalisation) \mathrm{tr}(\Phi) = n_{\mathrm{target}}.

The dual program determines the matrix shadow prices:

  \max_{y_0, (y_\lambda \ge 0)} \quad n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0

subject to the matrix inequality:

  y_0 \cdot I \;+\; \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \cdot \pi_\lambda \;-\; T
  \;\preceq\; 0.

At the generic q optimum, strong duality holds and complementary slackness applies as a matrix equation.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring.
prf:confinement-sdp:
Proof Proof of confinement sdp. Sketch.

The program is a semidefinite program over the symmetric cone \mathbb{S}_+^N, N = \dim_R H_n(R, q), and existence/attainment of the optimum is standard convex duality.

  1. The feasible set is a compact spectrahedron and the objective is bounded below. The normalisation \mathrm{tr}(\Phi) = n_{\mathrm{target}} together with \Phi \succeq 0 confines \Phi to a bounded slice of the PSD cone, on which the linear objective \langle T, \Phi\rangle attains its minimum \Phi^\star \succeq 0.

  2. Slater \Rightarrow strong duality. Under the strict-feasibility hypothesis (a \Phi_0 \succ 0 strictly satisfying every per-block and 2\times2 pair constraint, available at generic q where |q + q^{-1}| > 0), the conic-duality theorem gives strong duality — the dual SDP is solvable, \mathrm{primal} = \mathrm{dual}, and the complementary-slackness identity \Phi^\star(y_0^\star I + \sum_\lambda y_\lambda^\star \pi_\lambda - T) = 0 certifies optimality ([boyd-vandenberghe-2004], §5.9). The shadow prices y_\lambda^\star \ge 0 are exactly the per-block Frobenius-positivity duals of the LP/SDP witness contract.

The result is conditional on the strict-feasibility (Slater) hypothesis, and the conic-duality step is cited from the standard theory rather than proved here. \square
rem:sdp-degeneracy-at-metallic-coinciden:
Remark SDP degeneracy at cost-coincidence detects the metallic-ratio ladder. Observation. At the cost-coincidence loci of the operator-selection LP/SDP—points q^* > 0 where two cost coefficients t_i(q) and t_j(q) become equal—the strict-complementarity condition fails and the SDP is degenerate. These loci coincide exactly with the metallic-ratio ladder \{\delta_n : n \in \mathbb{N}^+\}.

The mechanism. For the n=2 LP with basis \{\gamma, \sigma_0\} of H_2(q), the cost coefficients are

  t_1(q) \;=\; 2(q + q^{-1}),
  \qquad
  t_2(q) \;=\; q^2 - q^{-2}.

A direct algebraic calculation gives

  t_1(q) \;=\; t_2(q)
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  q - q^{-1} \;=\; 2
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  q \;=\; \delta_{\rm silver} \;=\; 1 + \sqrt{2}.

At this q, the LP optimum is a face of the feasible polytope, not a vertex. Any feasible x satisfying x_1 + x_2 = n_{\rm target} achieves the same primal cost t_1 x_1 + t_2 x_2 = t_1 \cdot n_{\rm target}. The dual shadow prices y_i^* become non-unique (multiple optimal (y_0^*, y^*) values), strict complementarity fails, and the active set \mathcal{A} = \{i : y_i^* > 0\} is empty. This is the SDP-degeneracy signature: rapid loss of conditioning, ambiguous identification of binding constraints, and multiple optimal solutions returned.

Empirical verification. The n=2 LP active-set sweep observed this signature. Below silver the active set was \{0\} (row 1 tight), AT silver it was \emptyset (degenerate), above silver it was \{1\} (row 2 tight). The degeneracy at silver is the first non-null result in a series of prior canonical probes that all returned smooth observables.

Structural significance. The metallic-ratio ladder sits on the algebraic side: q = \delta_n is where the Hecke scalar q - q^{-1} takes the integer value n, making \sigma satisfy the integer-coefficient quadratic \sigma^2 = n \sigma + 1. Smooth observables (Wenzl weights, Jones polynomial signs, n=3 per-block character signs) do not see this discrete arithmetic structure because they are rational functions of q with no discontinuities. The LP-vertex combinatorics sees it: cost-coefficient coincidences are algebraic events that translate the arithmetic of q - q^{-1} into a topological change of the optimum's face dimension.

Physical interpretation. Identifying the silver coincidence with the CFL phase transition of dense quark matter gives the empirical handle on this algebraic phenomenon. The CFL transition density \rho_c is the physical realization of the silver-coincidence point. The SDP degeneracy there is the order-parameter discontinuity of the first-order CFL transition. Multiple metallic ratios on the ladder correspond to multiple phase transitions. The bar-mirror \varphi^2 \approx 2.618 of the deconfinement boundary q_{\rm gold} = 1/\varphi^2 forms a candidate for the CFL \to gCFL boundary observed in dense-QCD phenomenology.

Generalisation (conditional). For the strand-n LP with basis size d_n = n!, the cost coefficients t_i(q) are rational functions of q. The pairwise coincidence equations t_i(q) = t_j(q) have rational-function solutions. Those solutions on the metallic ladder constitute the set S(n) \subseteq \{\delta_k : k \le n\} of LP-degeneracy points for n strands. For n=2, S(2) = \{2\} (silver only). For n=3, the categorical evaluation returns \{\delta_{\rm silver}\}. The higher-strand characterisation remains conditional.

Running an SDP solver on the canonical operator-selection problem at q-values near each metallic ratio reveals measurable signs of degeneracy: rising condition-number of the KKT system, multiple optimal solutions reported by the solver, and y_i^* values dropping to tolerance for all i simultaneously. Each observation tests the algebraic identification.
prop:universal-braid-branching:

  \chi(K, \lambda)
  = f^{\lambda/[3]} \cdot \chi_K^{\mathrm{sym}}
  + f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]} \cdot \chi_K^{\mathrm{std}}
  + f^{\lambda/[1^3]} \cdot \chi_K^{\mathrm{alt}}

where f^{\lambda/\mu} = |\mathrm{SYT}(\lambda/\mu)| counts saturated chains from \mu to \lambda in Young's lattice. The three base characters compute once from the Hoefsmit seminormal form:

Knot K \chi_K^{\mathrm{sym}} \chi_K^{\mathrm{std}} \chi_K^{\mathrm{alt}}
4_1 (figure-eight) 1 2 - [3]_q 1
B_3 (Borromean) 1 (2 - [3])([3]^2 - 4[3] + 1) 1
unknot (identity) 1 2 1

prf:universal-braid-branching:
Proof Proof of universal braid branching. The braid K lives in H_3(R, q) (generators T_1, T_2). The representation \rho_\lambda of H_k(R, q) restricts to H_3(R, q) via the standard inclusion H_3(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_k(R, q) (using the first two generators). The branching rule gives:

  \rho_\lambda \!\downarrow_{H_3}
  = \bigoplus_{\mu\,\vdash\,3} f^{\lambda/\mu} \cdot \rho_\mu

Taking characters and using additivity yields the formula.

Base characters (symbolic proofs).

Figure-eight. 4_1 = T_1 T_2^{-1} T_1^{-1} T_2 is the commutator [T_1, T_2^{-1}]. In the symmetric and alternating channels (\dim = 1), the eigenvalue products are q \cdot q^{-1} \cdot q^{-1} \cdot q = 1 and (-q^{-1})(-q)(-q)(-q^{-1}) = 1 respectively.

  = \alpha^2 - h\alpha + \gamma^2 - h\gamma
    - (q^2 + q^{-2})(\alpha\gamma + 1)

  = -\alpha\gamma(1 + [3]) - ([3] - 1)

prop:eigenvalue-product-expansion:
Proposition Eigenvalue product expansion of the nuclear braid Markov trace. For a nucleus with Z protons and N neutrons (A = Z + N), the symmetric channel eigenvalue product of the nuclear braid in the [2{,}1] representation of H_3(R, q) is:

  \Lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}
  = q^{(Z-N)(A-1)/2} \cdot \Bigl(\frac{[2]_q}{2}\Bigr)^{\!ZN}

Its logarithm expands in the isospin variable T = |Z - N|/2 as:

  = \ell_2 \cdot \frac{A^2}{4}
  \;+\; \ell \cdot T \cdot A
  \;-\; \ell \cdot T
  \;-\; \ell_2 \cdot T^2

where \ell = \ln q and \ell_2 = \ln([2]_q/2).

nn (\sigma^{-1}) (1, -h) q^{-1} -q

  \qquad

Verified against explicit Hoefsmit matrix computation for all N = Z nuclei (T = 0: {}^4\mathrm{He}, {}^6\mathrm{Li}, {}^{12}\mathrm{C}, {}^{16}\mathrm{O}) to machine precision.

def:habiro-ring:
Definition Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. Let R = \mathbb{Z}[q]. The q-Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}_q is the inverse limit of the polynomial rings R / ( (q; q)_n ) as n \to \infty, where (q; q)_n = \prod_{k=1}^n (1 - q^k) is the q-Pochhammer symbol:

  \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}_q
  \;:=\;
  \varprojlim_n \frac{\mathbb{Z}[q]}{((q; q)_n)}.
rem:habiro-ring-remark:
Remark Elements and role of the Habiro ring. Elements of the q-Habiro ring are formal power series of the form \sum_{n=0}^\infty c_n(q) \, (q; q)_n with c_n \in \mathbb{Z}[q].

The Habiro ring completes the polynomial ring \mathbb{Z}[q] at the cyclotomic ideals. It forms the natural home for quantum topological invariants evaluated at roots of unity, where the terms (q; q)_n vanish for n large enough, truncating the infinite series to a finite sum.

Application to QOU. The algebraic quantum volume evaluates as a finite sum precisely because its components belong to a generalized Habiro ring where the truncation depth connects to the physical shell structure.
cor:habiro-expansion-atomic:
Corollary Atomic-braid Habiro expansion: integrality and termination. The algebraic quantum volume of a confined atom \mathfrak{H} admits a q-Habiro expansion:

  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{alg}}(\mathfrak{H})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{n=0}^N c_n(q) \, (q; q)_n

where the truncation depth N correlates with the number of valence nucleons.

This proposition guarantees that the binding energy formula terminates algebraically when evaluated at a root of unity. The coefficients c_n(q) determine the specific shell contributions. This structure bridges the categorical operator traces to the empirical magic-shell mass phenomenology.

For a knot, the expansion of this shape is Habiro's. The colored Jones polynomials are J_n(q) = \sum_{k \ge 0} c_{n,k}(q)\,H_k(q) with H_k(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm1}] and a knot-independent cyclotomic kernel c_{n,k}(q) = q^{-kn}(q^{n+1};q)_k\,(q^{n-1};q^{-1})_k that vanishes for k \ge n \ge 1, so the sum terminates at each color; at n = 0 the same sum defines an element of the Habiro ring, and replacing q^n by a variable gives an element of the colored Habiro ring [garoufalidis-kashaev-descendants2023, §2.2, eqs. The same paper records a second realization of the colored Jones polynomials through R-matrices at roots of unity built from solutions of the pentagon identity [garoufalidis-kashaev-descendants2023, Abstract and §3]. Both statements concern knot invariants; the application of the expansion to \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{alg}}(\mathfrak{H}) and the reading of N above are made here and are not in that source.
def:z-habiro-ring:
Definition z-Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][z]}_z. Let R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][z].   \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}][z]}_z

rem:z-habiro-ring-remark:

  \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}^{\mathrm{trans}}(\beta)

  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \Phi_q(z_i),

where z_i = |\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}| are the per-generator additive Wedderburn traced-volume magnitudes, and \Phi_q is the quantum dilogarithm.

  2. q-Habiro completion, regularizing in q, not z.

  n_\star \;:\; \{\text{confined particles}\} \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{N}_{\geq 1},
  \qquad

derivable from QOU aether data alone, such that the cyclotomic projection evaluated at q = q_0 and z = z_i recovers the empirical brane-tower contribution to the binding B(\mathfrak{H}) uniformly across atoms.

If true, the conjecture:

  2. Promotes Yekutieli truncation to a structural cyclotomic projection at a canonical level.

def:two-row-stratum:
Definition Two-row Wedderburn stratum \Lambda^2(n) := \{\lambda \vdash n : \ell(\lambda) \le 2\}. Let H_n(q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra on n strands. It admits the canonical Wedderburn decomposition

  H_n(q) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda)

indexed by partitions \lambda \vdash n. The two-row stratum contains the partitions with at most two parts:

  \Lambda^2(n) \;:=\; \{\, \lambda \vdash n : \ell(\lambda) \le 2 \,\}
  \;=\; \{\, (n-k, k) : 0 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor \,\}.

Structural significance

The two-row stratum carries the \mathrm{SU}(2) Schur–Weyl image. Restrict to the \mathrm{SU}(2) action:

  H_n(q) \;\twoheadrightarrow\; \mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{SU}(2)}\!\bigl(V^{\otimes n}\bigr),
\quad V = \mathbb{C}^2.

Partitions with \ell(\lambda) > 2 map to zero. They correspond to higher-rank symmetry components absent from the \mathrm{SU}(2) spin-pairing observable. The q-deformed spin observables, including the magic-shell stabilisation coupling, live strictly in the two-row sector.

Scope of the two-row stratum: it is the whole support, in the trace and in the binding sum alike. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) the restriction is not a dominance but an identity. The Wenzl weight satisfies y_\lambda = 0 exactly when \ell(\lambda) \geq 3, because the Schur–Weyl fibre is the two-dimensional fundamental of \mathrm{SU}_q(2); so every \ell(\lambda) > 2 term of \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda vanishes, and so does every \ell(\lambda) > 2 term of the binding sum \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda \Delta_\lambda — the factor \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)} f^\lambda multiplies a weight that is already zero. The binding sum therefore does inherit the restriction, at every A, exactly.

Two-row concentration. While \Delta_\lambda in isolation grows largest on balanced many-row diagrams, at z = q^3/(q^2+1) all weights with \ell(\lambda) > 2 vanish identically (y_\lambda = 0), so only the two-row stratum \Lambda^2(n) contributes to the ordinary Markov trace.

Indexing the stratum

Then |\Lambda^2(n)| = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1. For the ^4\mathrm{He} strand count (n = 12), there are 7 partitions:

\Lambda^2(12) = \{(12), (11,1), (10,2), (9,3), (8,4), (7,5), (6,6)\}.

Distinguished partitions include:

  • \lambda = (n): the trivial representation. It is one-dimensional, V_{(n)} = \mathbb{C}.
  • \lambda = (n-1, 1): the standard representation. It has dimension n - 1.
  • Self-conjugate \lambda \in \Lambda^2(n): this is only (n/2, n/2) for even n, the balanced two-row partition. For n = 12, this is (6, 6).

The non-self-conjugate partitions (n-k, k) with k < n/2 form mirror pairs under the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1}. The conjugate partition (n-k, k)' exits \Lambda^2(n), so each (n-k, k) pairs with itself under the involution.

Empirical use

The per-partition decomposition is c_\lambda := y_\lambda(q_0) \cdot \chi^\lambda_q(\beta_{^4\mathrm{He}}) across all 77 partitions of 12. The two-row stratum \Lambda^2(12) carries the total trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{^4\mathrm{He}}) exactly — 100\,\%, not as a measurement but as an identity, since y_\lambda = 0 for the 70 partitions of 12 with \ell(\lambda) > 2.

The same pattern holds across the \{D, T, {}^3\mathrm{He}, {}^4\mathrm{He}\} series. The dominant block for each atom always lies in \Lambda^2(3A).
def:two-row-projection:

  \pi_{\mathrm{2-row}} \;\colon\; H_n(q) \;\to\;
